Hey there @kennedyshead, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`asuswrt`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L49) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@ollo69  I don't actually think the disconnect call is necessary right? Especially as it seems that the ssh connection also doesn't need the disconnect.

If it is really necessary a comment as to why it's necessary might be valuable for future developers.

I put the call because API telnet connection provide it (ssh connection does not). 
Because ConfigFlow open a connection and a new one is opened by integration immediately after, it seemed logic using API method to close the existing one.
But is not a problem to completely remove this call if is clear that is not useful and that the router can manage multiple connection without issue.

I think the disconnect call during configuration can be removed, the library should handle a new connection properly (in my opinion). The one during `close` is good to keep, but I'll add a disconnect to the Ssh version as well, once that is upstream this close method can be simplified to just do the disconnect.

Fine, I will change the code as you suggested, adding a comment in `close` method. I see in your fork that disconnect method is `async`, so code and related test will need adjustment in future `aioasuwrt` release.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.3.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2021.2.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

asuswrt

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/asuswrt/

# old working config from 2021.2.3, now deprecated
asuswrt:
  host: 192.168.1.1
  username: ***
